data.narrative:
QuantWare, a Series B quantum computing company founded by Matt Rijlaarsdam and Alessandro Bruno, has raised $178M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Valuation analysis is constrained by limited comparable data. The peer-median method is not applicable: while 5 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy tight filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier positioning—a minimum of 3 comparable datapoints is required for reliable median-based triangulation. Accordingly, stage-progression methodology was applied, using QuantWare's $178M total raised as a base proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $338M.

The triangulated range spans $287M (low) to $389M (high), centered on $338M. This analysis rests on a single methodological pillar—stage-progression—which introduces material sensitivity to the assumed multiplier. Key uncertainties include the appropriate step-up magnitude for quantum computing specifically (where capital intensity and development timelines may differ from broader venture cohorts) and the relevance of the public comparables given their distinct market positioning and maturity. Narrower peer data at QuantWare's exact stage and technical focus would strengthen confidence in this range.
